newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT earnings tumble, sees better 1997.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT earnings tumble, sees better 1997.

text.p: Dutch paper, packaging and office products group KNP BT reported on Wednesday sharply lower fourth quarter and full year profits but said it expected an improvement in its earnings from operations in 1997.
Fourth quarter net profit from ordinary operations dived to 92 million guilders ($48.6 million) from 151 million in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Over the year net profit from ordinary operations more than halved to 231 million from 545 million guilders.
The company said restructuring measures it had taken or which were still in progress would bear fruit in 1997.

"The various measures that have been taken and that are being developed respectively, are to lead to a structural improvement of profitability, and will already in 1997 contribute to a material improvement of the result on ordinary operations," it said in a statement with the results.

However, it was unclear whether a modest recovery in paper prices would continue this year. "In the fourth quarter of 1996 paper prices showed only a slight rise despite healthy demand. It is not clear whether this recovery will continue in 1997," it said.
KNP BT said that as long as the paper market did not deteriorate it expected operational results in 1997 of its majority owned KNP Leykam paper unit to recover.

The company was more upbeat about prospects for its distribution and packaging operations. "Both sectors offer good potential for further growth in their core activities and an attractive return," it said.
KNP BT said Leykam's operating results recovered slightly in the fourth quarter, helped by rising sales volumes and prices.
"During the last quarter, volumes resulted in good utilisation of machines and there was evidence of a slight rise in paper prices," it said.
Paper production activities posted a fourth quarter profit of 26 million guilders, down from 84 million in the year-earlier period but up from a seven million guilder loss in the 1996 third quarter.

Fourth quarter paper sales volumes amounted to 322,000 tonnes, down from 349,000 tonnes in the year-earlier period. But the comparison was skewed by the inclusion of KNP BT's paper mill in Bruck, Austria, in the 1995 figures, the firm said.
The mill was divested in late 1995. KNP BT said that it had been forced to fully write off the performance-related portion of the Bruck sale.
KNP Leykam booked a full-year operating loss of five million guilders last year, after posting record operating profits of 375 million guilders in 1995.
Divestments accounted for around 60 million guilders of the decline, KNP BT said.
